page: OVHcloud l4-90 is a GPU-accelerated virtual instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. The system provides 22 dedicated physical cores on an x86_64 AMD EPYC 9454 processor clocked at 2.75 GHz without multithreading enabled. The CPU configuration includes AVX-512 extensions (including VNNI and BF16) alongside SHA-NI and AES hardware acceleration. Memory is provisioned at 90.0 GB, allocating roughly 4.09 GB per core. The instance incorporates an integrated 400 GB NVMe SSD for high-speed local data persistence and maintains an 8 Gbps baseline network interface. Public IPv4 connectivity is not included by default.

Hardware acceleration is anchored by a single NVIDIA L4 GPU from the Ada Lovelace generation, equipped with 24 GB of dedicated VRAM. In benchmark evaluations, this configuration demonstrates top-tier throughput for small and medium language model inference, delivering 2286.1 prompt tokens per second and 54.36 generation tokens per second on 7B parameter models. Host compute metrics show top-tier single-core performance in stress-ng tests and strong execution across Geekbench single-core and PassMark extended instruction suites.

System memory bandwidth benchmarks fall into middle-tier ranges, delivering 56.05 GB/sec sequential reads and 36.88 GB/sec writes under un-cached 256MB blocks. While large-scale 70B parameter models face VRAM capacity bottlenecks that constrain text generation, the instance achieves high efficiency for sub-24GB workloads. The single-socket density provides balanced computational resource distribution without over-provisioning memory or storage, optimizing cost per inference stream.

OVHcloud l4-90 is suited for real-time generative AI inference, computer vision pipelines, multi-stream video transcode operations, and general machine learning evaluation workloads requiring sustained dedicated CPU execution alongside modern GPU tensor architectures.

Hardware acceleration is provided by a single NVIDIA Ada Lovelace L4 GPU with 24 GB of VRAM. Networking features an 8 Gbps baseline link, with zero included public IPv4 addresses. Benchmark testing highlights top-tier single-core CPU throughput and top-tier inference speeds for small to mid-sized language models, achieving over 2280 prompt tokens per second on 7B models. Multithreaded decompression and vector instruction execution remain strong, while uncached memory throughput operates at average tiers. The system balances dedicated compute cores and power-efficient GPU acceleration, making it an efficient platform for machine learning inference, computer vision processing, and accelerated media encoding tasks.
